channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: The Alternative Aesthetic: Chance at the Margins · PhotoSC
item.description: PhotoSC is a non-profit photography gallery in Columbia, South Carolina, built around a continuing dialogue about photography and the photographic canon. Marking photography's 200 years of experimentation, The Alternative Aesthetic: Chance at the Margins goes looking for the accident and the sleight of hand — the idea that chance has sat at the heart of photographic and scientific discovery from the very beginning, and that the non-traditional method has always been the alternative to the cultural order of photography. The call seeks historical techniques, photosensitive chemicals and unusual materials, and the textures, colours and effects that are impossible with standard digital or silver gelatin work; experimentation is explicitly encouraged. The juror is Michael Kirchoff, Editor-in-Chief of Analog Forever Magazine, founding editor of Catalyst: Interviews, an ongoing juror for Photolucida's Critical Mass and a former board member of APA/LA. Photographers may submit up to five works for $35, with submissions open from 5 August to 13 September 2026 and accepted artists notified by 4 October. Accepted work must be printed no smaller than 8×10 inches and no larger than 16×20, framed and ready to hang, and delivered by the 23 October receipt-of-work date on the call timeline (a line of prose lower down the same page still says 30 September, which predates the 4 October notification). The exhibition opens 29 October at 918 Lady Street, Columbia, with a reception the same evening, and hangs until 29 November 2026. Sales are encouraged at a 40/60 gallery/artist split; photographers retain copyright. No AI-generated imagery is accepted. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Seed Prize for Emerging Photographers 2026 · National Emerging Art Prize
item.description: The National Emerging Art Prize was founded in 2021 to give Australia's most promising emerging visual artists a national platform, and in 2025 it expanded into contemporary photography with a dedicated category — The Seed Prize for Emerging Photographers, sponsored by Seed Funds Management, now in its second year. The winner receives a $10,000 acquisitive cash prize, a solo exhibition at The Garden Gallery presented by Michael Reid Northern Beaches in 2027, and mentoring sessions with NEAP curator Amber Creswell Bell and the Michael Reid directors. NEAP is curated by Amber Creswell Bell, a writer and curator known for championing emerging Australian artists across a run of best-selling books on Australian art; she sits on the selection panel and works with the selected artists to curate the finalists' exhibition. The 2026 panel includes artists Tom Polo and Tamara Dean, Head On Photo Festival founder Moshe Rosenzveig OAM, Belle editor-in-chief Tanya Buchanan, Good Weekend senior writer Katrina Strickland, Decus founder Alexandra Donohoe Church, and collectors Edwina Bartholomew and Nicole Redden. There is no theme. The category is open to film and digital photographs presented as still, two-dimensional works, completed in 2025 or 2026. Prints must be at least 20cm square and no larger than 100cm on the longest side, editioned no higher than 15 (8 + 2AP recommended), and priced no higher than $3,000 unframed; finalists send work in tubes and it is exhibited unframed, pinned directly to the gallery wall, with NEAP retaining 50% of any sale. Artists must reside primarily in Australia and count as emerging — that is, not represented by a major commercial gallery; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists are encouraged to apply. There is no limit on entries per artist, but each work is submitted separately at $35. Finalists are announced 1 October and exhibited 29 October to 11 November 2026 at The Garden Gallery in Sydney's Royal Botanic Garden, with all work for sale. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: A$35 per work. Prize: A$10,000 + Solo exhibition + Mentoring.

item.title: Windows on the World · Click! Photography Festival
item.description: Click! Photography Festival turns downtown Raleigh into a month-long photography city every October, spreading exhibitions, talks and screenings across Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill. Windows on the World is its storefront show: selected photographs are printed by the festival and installed in and around the shop windows of City Market, the historic brick market district in downtown Raleigh, so the work is met by people walking past rather than by gallery visitors. The theme is JOY, and the call asks what joy looks like to you — a fleeting smile, a quiet landscape, a family celebration, an unexpected encounter, a moment of personal triumph. All genres are welcome, from documentary and street photography to portraits, landscapes, abstract and experimental imagery, and all photographic processes are accepted: alternative, film or digital. The call is open to photographers of all levels, from emerging talents to seasoned professionals, and international submissions are accepted. Entry is $45 for up to five images. Artists do not ship work: everything selected is printed and displayed by the festival, with the possibility of a projection event on First Friday. The exhibition runs 1–31 October 2026 with an opening reception on Friday 2 October, and images not selected for the outdoor Plein Air exhibition are eligible for a travelling slide show presented around the Triangle through October. AI-generated images are not eligible. — Deadline: August 24, 2026. Fee: $45/5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Click! Plein Air
item.description: Click! Plein Air is the flagship outdoor exhibition of the Click! Photography Festival, the month-long October festival spread across Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill in North Carolina. For 2026 it moves from Moore Square, where the 2025 edition showed 35 photographers, to Dix Park — the 300-acre former state hospital campus that is now Raleigh's largest public park — where photographs are shown in the open air rather than on gallery walls. There is no set theme: photographers submit into open categories, and the festival is looking for striking, engaging work that holds up in front of a broad public audience outdoors. The festival's own page lists seven — abstract, documentary, landscape, people, creatures, street photography and still life — while the Smarter Entry form shows six, with portrait in place of people and creatures, so check the list when you upload. The call is open to photographers of all levels and to all photographic processes, alternative, film or digital, with international submissions accepted. Entry is $45 for up to five images, each of which must be titled. The juror is Jerome De Perlinghi. Jury selections are made by 6 September, the exhibition runs 1–31 October 2026, and the opening reception is on First Friday, 2 October. Images not selected for the outdoor exhibition remain eligible for a travelling slide show presented at venues throughout the Triangle during October. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: $45/5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SELF PORTRAITS 2026 · Matt Ford Studio
item.description: Matt Ford Studio is a photographer-run gallery and studio in Hackney Downs Studios, east London, whose programme leans toward sexuality, gender, identity and fashion. SELF PORTRAITS 2026 is its winter open call, exhibition and photo book, put together by Matt Ford after he began making self-portraits as a way of working through his own fears about AI, politics and the future of an artistic career, and became interested in self-portraiture itself — as vanity, as creativity, as self-expression, or simply as a record of where you are in your life. The call invites photographers worldwide to reflect on what it means to be human in the second quarter of the 21st century. Anyone 18 or over from any country may enter, at any level of skill, and both digital and analogue work is welcome — disposable cameras, phones and high-end DSLRs alike — along with collage and experimental work that still involves some element of self-portrait. Digitally enhanced images are accepted; AI-generated images are not. Judging for finalists and winners is done by the editors of ZERO.NINE Magazine. The winner receives £500 cash, the cover of the SELF PORTRAITS photo book, an 'On The Radar' feature in ZERO.NINE and a feature about their work; all semi-finalists appear in the photo book at no extra cost, and finalists are shown in the exhibition at the studio. Entry is £13 for the first photograph and £6 for each one after; if you reach the exhibition a further £20 per photograph shown covers printing (arranged with theprintspace) and exhibition admin, or you may send your own print at your own postage cost. Semi-finalists are announced 9 November, the book launch, private view and winners announcement is 10 December, and the exhibition is open to the public 11–14 December 2026. Work is for sale during the show, with 75% to the artist. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: £13 for 1 image, £6 each additional (£20 per print if selected). Prize: £500 + Exhibition + Photobook.

item.title: Liquida Winter Edition 2026 — Single Photo
item.description: Liquida Photofestival is the photography strand of Paratissima, the independent contemporary art event that has run in Turin since 2005 and is now one of the anchors of Turin Art Week. Its Winter Edition is the autumn spin-off of the main April festival, curated by Liquida's artistic director Laura Tota — an independent curator who has worked on Paratissima's photography programme since 2017 and is Exhibition Coordinator at PhEST, Photolux and Cortona On The Move. Single Photo is a new section for 2026: rather than a project, it asks for individual frames. Each entrant may submit between one and five photographs, which need not belong to the same body of work or even to the same line of research, and there is no set theme — the point is to leave photographers the widest possible margin of expression. Ten winning shots are chosen and shown as a collective exhibition inside the Liquida Winter Edition section, with each selected image coming from a different artist. The €25 participation fee is the only cost: Paratissima covers production, transport, shipping, installation and de-installation of the selected works, and the fee also includes the exhibition layout, wall captions, inclusion in the official ISBN catalogue, an artist badge and support for online and on-site sales. The catalogue itself is optional at €20 a copy. The festival runs 30 October – 1 November 2026 at the Real Collegio Carlo Alberto in Moncalieri, just outside Turin; the 2025 edition drew more than 20,000 visitors. Results are announced 12 September. Note that Liquida's separate Exhibition call, for full projects, works on a paid-wall-space model and is not this call. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Thin Air Magazine Issue 33 — The Oasis
item.description: Thin Air is a print literary and arts magazine produced by graduate students in the MFA programme at Northern Arizona University in Flagstaff, and it is reading visual art for its 33rd print issue, themed 'The Oasis'. The editors take the dictionary definition — a fertile green area in an arid region; something that provides refuge, relief or pleasant contrast — and push at it: in a turbulent and at times desolate world, what is your oasis, where do you seek shelter, and what spaces sustain you? They are equally interested in the conditions that produce an oasis, since one can only exist when surrounded by a severe lack of something crucial to survival — so what is your desert, and what drives you to look for relief? The call also asks whether an oasis can be a form of resistance, thinking of the sanctuaries that form in the midst of violence, fear and escalating political tension. For this issue the editors are specifically looking for art, photography and comics that represent the notion of the oasis, with an interest in pieces that work as full-page spreads as well as graphic narratives and poetry comics; outsider art is always welcome, as is anything that surprises or subverts expectations. Colour submissions are open, with particular interest in high-contrast pieces that capture the shades and hues of the oasis. Photographers may send up to five pieces at a minimum of 300dpi with a short description of each work and a two to five sentence bio. Submitting visual art is free — the written-genre categories carry a $3 reading fee that visual art does not — and only unpublished work is considered, though simultaneous submissions are encouraged. Reading begins in August each year and runs until the deadline. One restriction to note: Thin Air does not accept work from anyone affiliated with Northern Arizona University within the last seven years. — Deadline: October 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Rawhead Issue 04 — Visual Art
item.description: Rawhead is an independent online journal of art and literature named after one of the folkloric bogeymen used to frighten children into obedience — a deliberate choice, since the editors read monsters as mirrors that force us to confront realities more disturbing than whatever lurks in the dark, and read art as a form of resistance. It is not a horror publication, but it is interested in work that unsettles through emotional depth, sharp craft and surprising clarity. Rawhead is open for its fourth issue across poetry, visual art, fiction, creative nonfiction and hybrid work; submissions considered for Issue 04 may also be held for Issue 05. The visual art category takes three to ten pieces in any medium, explicitly including photography alongside illustration, digital collage, mixed media, painting and sculpture, uploaded as high-quality images of at least 1500px. The art editor is looking for work that explores the delicate threshold between fear and beauty — not horror or gore, but work that dances along the edges of heightened emotion, citing Louise Bourgeois, Francis Bacon, Man Ray, Joseba Eskubi, Anna Weyant and Jinyoung Yu as touchstones. Each issue Rawhead selects at least one outstanding artist and one standout writer for its Editor's Spotlight, a $100 award; every accepted piece is considered. Submission is free and the journal states it is fully committed to always offering free submissions, with optional paid expedited and priority response tiers that have no bearing on editorial decisions. Simultaneous submissions are accepted, and AI-generated content is not. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + $100.

item.title: Photobooks in Dialogue · Centrum för fotografi
item.description: Centrum för fotografi (CFF), Sweden's member organisation for photographers, is calling for photobooks and zines for an exhibition in Gothenburg staged with Fotobok Gbg as part of Fotobok Fest. The curators are looking for photo-based publications in which dialogue, collaboration or exchange are central: an exchange of ideas between two photographers, between an artist and an archive, between image and text, or the close interplay of artist, designer and publisher. They describe it as a ping-pong match, where ideas bounce from one side to the other in fine balance without ever falling off the table — books and zines where the exchange between several voices is fundamental and has shaped the work from the ground up. The exhibition runs 25–27 September 2026 at the CFF gallery on Bangatan 10 in Gothenburg, with support from the City of Gothenburg and the Swedish Photographers' Association. Publications from anywhere in the world are welcome, but shipping to Sweden is at the applicant's own cost; books must arrive by 22 September. Applications are free and consist of a single PDF of no more than 10 MB containing a CV of up to two pages, a presentation of the publication of up to 300 words in Swedish or English, and 10–15 pages from the book. Selected participants are notified at the end of August. After the exhibition you can either donate your publication to the Hasselblad Foundation Library in Gothenburg or have it returned at CFF's expense. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Legacy Lives Here II · Project Row Houses
item.description: Project Row Houses, the community arts organisation founded in 1993 in Houston's Third Ward, invites artists aged 60 and over to submit work for the second edition of Legacy Lives Here, a multimedia exhibition celebrating the artistic voices of elders, wisdom-keepers and culture-shapers. The organisers are looking for work that reflects personal histories, cultural memory and the ongoing act of passing down knowledge through art, and the show is open to a wide range of mediums. Submissions close 11:59pm on Friday 28 August 2026 and selected artists are notified by the first week of September. The exhibition is on view in PRH's Community Gallery from 17 September to 17 October 2026. Applications are made through SlideRoom and there is no entry fee. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Sensory Seduction Volume 3 — Into the Void
item.description: Sensory Seduction is a Sydney-based independent print magazine and creative platform covering art, literature, music and culture, now open for its third volume, 'Into the Void: Exploration and Discovery'. The issue embraces all aspects of the unknown and invites work interpreting exploration and discovery in the contributor's own way — going on a journey, doing something for the first time, expansion, travel, investigating a mystery, emigration and immigration, unexpected detours, a chance encounter, embracing a new culture, taking a risk, a transitional period, getting lost, leaving your comfort zone, uncovering a secret. The magazine publishes original, unpublished work across disciplines including photography, digital art, collage, film stills and editorial work alongside essays, interviews, poetry and reviews; existing work is welcome as long as it has not been published before and fits the theme. Photographers and visual artists may submit up to six images with an artist statement and/or captions for each image, and hybrid submissions combining writing and images are accepted. Submission is free, via the magazine's online form, and every submission receives a response. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: FIGURES Mentorship & Dummy Book Program 2026/2027
item.description: FIGURES, the Slow & Contemporary Photography platform behind the FIG001 book, is running its mentorship and dummy book programme for a second year, and is looking specifically for projects at the very earliest stage of creation — you do not need to show a single finished picture of the project to apply, and projects that are already too advanced will not be considered. Program winners get twelve monthly 1.5-hour one-to-one online sessions with founder and editor-in-chief Nicolas Blanchadell, covering every phase from deepening the initial concept through production, picture editing and sequencing; a renowned guest artist/curator joins for one mid-programme session, and a professional art-book graphic designer steps in at the end to finalise the cover and the more demanding pages. Each winner leaves with a printed dummy book plus the ready-to-print PDF and all supporting material. The number of selections scales with entries: for every 150 valid submissions FIGURES picks one program winner plus ten further projects for a one-hour individual review. All photographic practices are welcome — documentary, portrait, street, experimental, fashion — as are mixed-media projects where photography is central to the process or makes up at least half the final work. Entry is €10, or free with the discounted purchase of the FIG001 issue at €25; no further fees are asked of selected artists, and applicants facing financial hardship are invited to write to FIGURES directly. If fewer than 150 valid applications arrive, the programme is cancelled and €10 entrants are refunded in full. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: €10 (or €25 with FIG001 issue). Prize: Mentorship and dummy book.

item.title: New Mexico Blue Bus Shelter Art · New Mexico Arts
item.description: New Mexico Arts' Art in Public Places programme, working with the North Central Regional Transit District's Art in Transit programme, is commissioning artists to create digital artwork to be printed onto perforated steel panels at three Blue Bus shelters in Taos, Española and Santa Fe. Selected artists create an original work — or digitise existing non-digital work — to fit a two- or three-panel shelter, each panel roughly 53 by 77 inches; all printing and installation is handled by NCRTD. The organisers ask for artwork that speaks to the local culture and community: cultural homelands, local languages, landscapes and agricultural practices, the diversity of lifeways, traditions and landmarks, and the artist's own lived experience and connection to the area. This is a request for qualifications, not a proposal call — do not make new work for it; submit up to ten images of completed artwork that demonstrate your style and technique, ideally digital work or work with local themes, plus an artist statement and answers on your transportation story and your connection to Northern New Mexico. Artists are paid $5,000 per completed artwork, inclusive of all fees and expenses. Entry is free. Open to all artists working in New Mexico, with preference given to those living in or with strong ties to Taos, Rio Arriba and Santa Fe counties; employees and family of employees of NMDCA or NCRTD are excluded. Selection is by the Art in Transit Committee, drawn from representatives across Northern New Mexico including Rio Arriba, Santa Fe, Taos and Los Alamos counties, Ohkay Owingeh and Taos Pueblo. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000 commission.

item.title: Louvre Unbound Magazine — Celebration Edition
item.description: A one-off anniversary edition marking Louvre Unbound's first year, published alongside an international event in Spain held with Luka Gallery for the inauguration of the gallery's new space inside the Castillo de Santiago, expected to draw 300–400 invited guests including curators, collectors, European press and cultural professionals. Selected artists are published in the Celebration Edition and also receive a two-month virtual exhibition, two months of promotion across the magazine's social channels, worldwide digital publication, global print-on-demand distribution via Peecho and Lulu, and a place on the printed event flyers handed to guests throughout the celebration. Submissions are open to visual artists worldwide working in any medium, photography included; submit up to four artworks through the magazine's Google Form. Submitting is free — participation fees apply only on acceptance, and for this edition alone they are quoted in euros: €89 for returning artists and €115 for new artists, covering a four-page featured-artist spread with one artwork per page plus contact links. Louvre Unbound states it is a non-profit platform and that the fee supports editorial work, design, printing and distribution. The edition will only be published if a minimum number of participating artists is reached; if it is cancelled, all registered artists are refunded in full. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free (€89–€115 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: UNFOLD — Cambridge Photography Gallery
item.description: Cambridge Photography Gallery's first annual physical exhibition, bringing together artists invited from its previous online shows alongside new voices found through this open call. Rather than setting a narrow theme, the gallery asks how your photography unfolds — as a story, a memory, a place, a relationship, an identity or a way of seeing. Some projects reveal themselves slowly while others leave questions unanswered; some look outward, others inward. Singles and series are both welcome and there is no right or wrong interpretation. Selected works are printed and presented as part of the group exhibition in Cambridge, UK, running 9 to 11 October 2026, and each participating artist receives a dedicated post on the gallery's Instagram and a digital certificate of participation. Submission is by email and free; a £30 participation fee applies only if your work is selected. For the selection stage files can be any size, format or orientation; selected artists are then asked for high-resolution files suitable for printing, around 300 ppi and at least 3000 pixels on the longest side. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free (£30 if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: HALFTONE Print Fair 2026 · PhotoIreland
item.description: The 12th edition of HALFTONE, PhotoIreland's annual print fair at The Library Project in Dublin's Temple Bar, running 28 November 2026 to 24 January 2027. Works are displayed salon-style and sold both at the venue and online at thelibraryproject.ie; the fair has raised almost €100,000 for artists since 2015 and supported the practice of over 800 participating artists, with sales to private, corporate and public collections. Applications are open to fine art printers, illustrators, designers, photographers and all visual artists and creatives, for works produced from 2024 onwards using any print technique — screenprint, stencil, risography, lithography, etching, inkjet printing and more — without any limitation of approach or concept. Submissions may include up to 10 artworks, with two images per work: the print itself and a photograph or mock-up showing it framed or mounted as it would be displayed. All submitted works must be available for sale. The gallery takes a 40% commission, which should be built into the price you submit, and artists invoice for the remaining 60% after the fair; PhotoIreland adds 13.5% VAT on top of the submitted price. Selected artists are contacted by 2 November 2026 and deliver work between 3 and 15 November, with unsold work collected 25 to 31 January 2027. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: €10 (free for International Centre for the Image members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Southwest Artists Series Purchase Initiative · New Mexico Arts
item.description: New Mexico Arts' Art in Public Places programme buys artwork outright for publicly accessible buildings across the state — amphitheatres, community centres, courthouses, educational institutions, fire stations, healthcare facilities, libraries, recreation complexes, rest areas and senior centres among them. The 2026 Southwest Artists Series Purchase Initiative aims to diversify the state collection by purchasing work from artists at every stage of their careers, and all media in all genres are considered; New Mexico Arts names photography explicitly among the mediums it accepts, alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, mosaic, graphic arts, etching, lithography, silkscreen, textile, fibre, wood, metal, glass, mixed media, collage and assemblage. Work must be durable, permanent, low-maintenance and compliant with ADA guidelines once installed, and suitable for interior or exterior display. The programme seeks artwork in the $5,000–$50,000 range, and the price must be all-inclusive: materials, labour, museum-quality framing under Plexiglas, security hangers, delivery, installation, insurance, taxes, commissions and both written and professional photographic documentation of the work. Since its inception in 1986 AIPP has placed more than 3,000 works of art across all 33 New Mexico counties, amounting to over $21 million paid directly to artists. Open to artists who reside in New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, Colorado, Oklahoma or Texas, and to galleries located in those states, which may submit on behalf of any artist they represent regardless of that artist's residency. A statewide Submission Review Committee of artists, arts professionals and community leaders scores applications, and the selected pool is then shown to local committees for purchase consideration. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000–$50,000 purchase.

item.title: Wellcome Photography Prize 2027 · Wellcome
item.description: Wellcome's biennial photography prize returns for 2027, open to everyone, everywhere, and free to enter. The prize brings photography and scientific imaging together around health and science: discovery research, mental health, infectious disease, and climate and health. There are three categories — Striking solo photography (a single photograph), A storytelling series (3–5 photographs), and The marvels of scientific and medical imaging (a single image made with a scientific or medical imaging technique). Each category winner receives £10,000, and a further 22 entries across the three categories are awarded £1,000 each; the prize draws extensive international media coverage and image makers may be invited to showcase their work at events. Eligible disciplines include documentary, clinical, studio and still-life photography, close-up photography and photomacrography, microscopy, and medical imaging such as CT, PET, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound and thermography, as well as new and emerging biomedical imaging technologies. Illustration, moving image and AI-generated images are not accepted. Images must have been taken after 31 December 2021 and submitted at print resolution. Judges weigh creativity and visual impact, storytelling and relevance, and technical excellence — the story behind an image counts as much as the image. Wellcome also publishes ethical storytelling guidelines developed with Eh!woza. Entries opened 14 July 2026; the top 25 entries and the winners are announced in summer 2027. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £10,000 per category + 22 × £1,000.

item.title: Open Call for Emerging Artists · Elliott Gallery
item.description: Elliott Gallery in Amsterdam is shifting its open-call programme away from exhibition proposals and towards early-career photographers: recent graduates of universities and photography courses, current students, and self-taught photographers in the early stages of their careers, worldwide. The gallery is explicit that it is not looking for flawless, finished portfolios but for fresh voices, raw talent, authenticity and potential. There is no set theme; the gallery looks for a distinct perspective and a genuine passion for the medium, and accepts photography only. The prize is a personalised mentorship with the Elliott Gallery curatorial team — three 60-minute one-to-one sessions over three months covering how to refine an artistic identity and conceptual approach through intensive portfolio reviews, how to navigate the fine art market, price work, write statements and approach galleries, and how to curate work for digital and physical spaces, with the distinct potential for further collaboration such as digital exhibitions, group shows and print sales. Shortlisted artists also receive exposure across the gallery's website and social channels to its base of fine art photography collectors. Applicants submit a single public link to a folder or online portfolio plus a statement of up to 500 words, via Google Forms. Applications opened 24 July 2026 and close 9 August; the shortlist is announced 14 August and the winner on 21 August 2026. The €25 fee covers administration costs. Elliott Gallery is a physical gallery at Tussen de Bogen 91 and complies with the Gallery Fair Practice Code. — Deadline: August 9, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Art Hop 2026 · Hill Country Arts Focus
item.description: Art Hop is a statewide juried exhibition run by Hill Country Arts Focus, a 501(c)(3) founded in 2007 to promote the arts in the northern Hill Country of central Texas. The 2026 edition runs the whole of October in Georgetown's historic downtown district, with selected work shown at the Georgetown Public Library and Lamppost Coffee, both just off the courthouse Square. Photography is one of six judged categories, alongside 2-D Representational, 2-D Abstract, 3-D Representational, 3-D Abstract and Digital Art; the photography category covers camera-generated photographic images. Awards run to $1,000 for Best in Show plus cash or prizes totalling almost $4,000 across the individual categories, announced at the reception ceremony. Judging happens in two rounds — online in late August, then in person before the exhibit opens, which determines placements and cash awards. Entry is $45 for up to three artworks or $55 for four or five, with a limit of five entries per artist, submitted through EntryThingy. Wall pieces including photography may be up to 48 inches on any side including the frame and must arrive ready to install with professional hardware. The call is open to any artist aged 16 or older residing in Texas. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $45 (up to 3 works), $55 (4–5). Prize: $1,000 Best in Show + category awards.

item.title: 110th Annual Open Juried Show · New Rochelle Art Association
item.description: The New Rochelle Art Association has run an annual juried show since 1912, when its first exhibition celebrated the opening of the city's new library and included work by sculptor Robert Aitken, painters G. Glenn Newell, Remington Schuyler and A.G. Heaton, and illustrators Norman Rockwell, Joseph C. Leyendecker and Victor Forsythe. The 110th edition is open to all artists 18 and over, with Photography one of the judged categories alongside Oil/Acrylic, Water Media, Graphics/Pastel, Mixed Media and Sculpture/Fine Craft. A minimum of $2,500 in cash awards is distributed across the categories. Each artist may submit up to two entries for a single fee of $35 ($30 for members); acceptance into the show automatically brings NRAA membership. All 2-D work must be suitably framed at least 0.75 inches deep — gallery-wrapped canvas is acceptable — wired and ready to hang, with no sawtooth hooks, and must not exceed 36 × 48 inches including the outside edge of the frame. Work is hand delivered rather than shipped. The exhibition runs 28 September to 1 November 2026 in the Lumen Winter Gallery at New Rochelle Public Library, open daily with library hours, with a reception on Sunday 18 October during New Rochelle's Arts Fest. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: $35 ($30 members). Prize: $2,500+ in cash awards.

item.title: The Art of the Automobile · Sacramento Fine Arts Center
item.description: A juried show at the Sacramento Fine Arts Center in Carmichael, California, open to all art media with an automobile theme, with events around the exhibition sponsored by the United British Sports Car Club Sacramento. The judge is Kandi Thompson, a Sacramento-area watercolour painter of thirty-five years who has studied with nationally and internationally acclaimed artists, been a member of several art groups including the California Watercolor Association, and been published in Watercolor Magic and the Artists Magazine calendar. Photography is specifically accommodated: the rules exclude giclées and works made by any commercial printing process, but state the exception for photography. Work must be original, finished in the last three years, not previously shown in a juried show at Sac Arts, and available for sale, with a maximum size of 4 × 8 feet; hanging pieces must be wired with D-rings, and works over 29 × 35 inches must use plastic rather than glass. Up to three pieces per artist may be submitted at $25 each or three for $60, dropping to $20/$50 for members and $15/$40 for youth entrants. The centre retains a 50% commission on sales for non-members and 30% for members. Jury decisions are sent on 21 August, and the exhibition runs 8 September to 3 October 2026. — Deadline: August 12, 2026. Fee: $25 each or 3 for $60 ($20/$50 members, $15/$40 youth). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Annual Show of Small Works 2026 · Parklane Gallery
item.description: Parklane Gallery's Annual Winter Show of Small Works is a seasonal favourite in Kirkland, Washington, timed to the holiday shopping season so that visitors can buy work and take it home immediately rather than waiting for the show to close. Parklane is a co-operative gallery whose programme covers painting, photography, sculpture, glasswork and jewellery, and the call is open to any 2-D or 3-D artwork not previously shown at the gallery. Awards are $500 for first place, $300 for second and $250 for third, plus honourable mentions, additional special recognition awards, and separate miniature awards for pieces that meet the definition and quality of a miniature. The juror is to be announced. Hanging work must be no larger than 13 inches in height or width and 3-D work no more than 6 inches in any dimension; there is no lower size limit, and accepted pieces with an image area under 25 square inches may be shown in a separate Miniatures section. Entry is $25 plus $5 per piece for up to seven pieces per artist. The show is both hung and online: the juror chooses prizes from all accepted pieces, every accepted work goes into the online store when the show starts, and because wall space is limited some pieces hang in November and others in December. Notifications go out 28 September, accepted work is due 16 October, and the exhibition runs 4 November 2026 to 2 January 2027. — Deadline: September 23, 2026. Fee: $25 + $5 per piece (up to 7). Prize: $500 + $300 + $250.

item.title: Small Works, Big Joy 2026 · Arts Center East
item.description: A curated show at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut celebrating the power of small-format art and the craftsmanship, creativity and precision that flourish within limited dimensions. The exhibition hangs in the Eureka Gallery from 12 November to 19 December 2026 and stays open through the centre's popular Annual Holiday Artisan Fair. All media are welcome including painting, drawing, sculpture, photography, mixed media, printmaking, ceramics, fiber, metal and textiles, so long as the work meets the size limit: no piece may exceed 12 inches in any dimension, and sculptural works must fit within a 12-inch cube. Artists are encouraged to price work under $200. Arts Center East's standing rules for juried exhibits apply — open to artists 18 and over, up to five pieces each, no work shown in a previous ACE juried exhibit, all work original with no kits and no AI-generated art, and nothing made under instruction in a class, workshop or lesson. Entry is $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), rising by $5 per additional piece up to five. Wall-hung work must be wired with two loops and professional picture wire; sawtooth hangers and frames with triangular tabs are refused on arrival. The centre takes a 35% commission on sales for non-members and 25% for ACE artist members. — Deadline: October 16, 2026. Fee: $35–$55. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: AUTO PHOTO Awards 2026 · Shutter Hub
item.description: The AUTO PHOTO Awards celebrate 100 global winners in automotive photography, with the Top 100 images printed in the annual AUTO PHOTO photobook published by Shutter Hub Editions. Past editions are held in international archives and collections including the British Library, Cambridge University and Motorsport UK HQ, and sold through selected stockists. There are no categories — entries are open to all photographers whatever their level of experience, with suggested prompts covering cars as art, motorsport, scenes and styling, innovation, and auto portraiture. Alongside the Top 100 there are eight named judges' awards, and a Creative Impact Award whose winner joins the judging panel. Pay-what-you-can entry from £25, 10 images per entry and unlimited entries; free submissions are offered on request to photographers experiencing homelessness, displacement, poverty or social injustice. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: £25+. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: Life Framer — Series Award Edition XII
item.description: Life Framer's annual series award, running alongside its twelve monthly themed competitions and asking instead for a cohesive body of work — any topic, any genre, any format. Submissions are a series of 5 to 20 photographs with a shared theme or aesthetic rather than a broad portfolio; images may be new or from the archive, and may have been previously published or exhibited. Edition XII is judged by Lisa Woodward and Mia Dalglish, co-curators at Pictura Gallery in Bloomington, Indiana. Three finalists are shortlisted and each receives an online portfolio review session with the curators before the first prize is chosen. The winner receives a three-month, fully funded solo show at Pictura Gallery in summer 2027, curated by Woodward and Dalglish, with printing, framing and curatorial costs covered by Life Framer and Pictura Gallery. Second and third prizes receive the review session plus write-ups on the Life Framer Journal and Pictura Gallery's Curious Photo Blog. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Funded solo exhibition at Pictura Gallery.

item.title: Solo Artist Exhibition Fall 2027 · Hill Center Galleries
item.description: Open call for artists from Washington DC, Maryland and Virginia to propose a solo exhibition at Hill Center at the Old Naval Hospital on Capitol Hill. Hill Center Galleries runs a yearly Solo Artist Exhibition in which roughly six artists each get a solo show installed concurrently in one of the galleries, sharing a joint opening reception, an artist panel talk and a holiday reception during the run. The Fall 2027 installation runs August 29, 2027 through January 9, 2028. Open to any 2D medium, including photography, that can hang on the Arakawa cable-and-hook system without extending more than six inches from the wall; there are no pedestals, tables or display cases. Applicants may submit existing work or propose a new body of work to be made for the show — submitted images are read as examples of the artist's practice. Work included must have been made in the last three years and not previously shown at Hill Center. All artwork must be available for sale. Open to artists 18 and over; the Galleries Director makes final determinations with input from jurors and colleagues. — Deadline: September 3, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Beyond Borders II: Global Voices · The Art Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at The Art Center in Johns Creek, Georgia exploring the complexity, nuance and lived experience of cultures around the world through deeply personal and authentic artistic perspectives. The call asks for work that reflects a global viewpoint not as a generalised or stereotypical concept but as something specific, individual and deeply felt — moving past simplified narratives and superficial multiculturalism toward the richness, tension, overlap and individuality within and between communities. Suggested themes include cultural heritage and identity, migration and diaspora, tradition and transformation, intersectionality and hybridity, cultural contrast and exchange, and personal narratives in a global context; entries may be celebratory, critical, bold or contemplative. Photography is among the eligible media, alongside mixed media, ceramics, drawing, fibre art, printmaking, painting, collage, digital art and sculpture. Juried by the curatorial staff of The Art Center. Up to three works for a $25 entry fee. On view September 11 – October 17, 2026, with an awards reception on the closing night. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $500 First Place.

item.title: Art of Abstraction · Arts Center East
item.description: Juried exhibition at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut inviting artists to explore the power of colour, shape, texture and movement beyond literal representation — from bold, expressive compositions to subtle, thought-provoking works, celebrating the many ways abstract art evokes emotion and invites personal interpretation. Photography is among the accepted media, alongside painting, mixed media, ceramics, sculpture, textiles, metal and illustration. Open to artists 18 and over; each artist may submit up to five pieces, and work must not have appeared in a previous ACE juried exhibit. No copies, no kits, no work made in a class and no AI-generated art. Entry is $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), rising per additional piece up to five. Shown in the Eureka Gallery, September 26 – October 31, 2026, with a reception and awards. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $35–$55. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Altered Horizons — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City, curated in-house by SaveArtSpace, opening October 9, 2026. Altered Horizons asks artists to disrupt the mundane landscape with visions of alternative realities, dream states and mind-expanding wonder — work that reawakens curiosity and sparks moments of lucid awareness for passers-by, whether through hyper-saturated surrealism, cosmic abstraction or visionary portraiture. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of any age, skill level or background; still images only, no video. Selected works are displayed on NYC ad space for at least one month; artists are notified after September 7, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in NYC.

item.title: Flatland Feature — Issue 3 · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: Online photography feature showcasing a series of a photographer's work in a slide-show format as a virtual gallery experience. Selected photographers' work is featured for six months on the MWCP website, January through June 2027. Each feature consists of 10–20 images with an accompanying artist statement and biography, and visitors can view and purchase photographs online (50% gallery commission). Selection is based on the thematic series submitted rather than on individual images. Open internationally to all subject matter, genre and photographic media — MWCP describes the feature as a platform for photographers making work about the central plains region and about the multitude of other places, ideas and concepts. No shipping is required; work is presented online only. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $100/10 images, $150/15, $200/20. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Identity 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of identity, which the gallery calls "a broad and versatile theme that can be explored through many photographic genres". Portraits can express personal or collective identity, documentary work can reveal the experiences of individuals or groups, and even landscapes or cityscapes can reflect the environments that shape who we are. Identity may be rooted in culture, religion, place, community or countless other influences, and photographers are invited to explore it in all its forms — whether reflecting their own or telling someone else's story. Selected work is shown at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 3 to 20 December 2026, and also appears in an online gallery on the gallery's website and in an exhibition catalogue. All selected participants receive a digital certificate of participation and are put forward for consideration as Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £38 participation fee that covers printing, installation and de-installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image. A discount is available to anyone selected for both December exhibitions. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on the shortest side) by free file transfer to the gallery's submissions address. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: Free (£38 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: In Between 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the in-between: "those fleeting moments that sit on the edge of change, right before something happens or just after it unfolds". The gallery is looking for images that hold tension and drama, capturing the charged pause between action and outcome. All photographic genres are welcome and the theme is open to interpretation — whatever the in-between means to you. Selected work is shown at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 3 to 20 December 2026, and also appears in an online gallery on the gallery's website and in an exhibition catalogue. All selected participants receive a digital certificate of participation and are put forward for consideration as Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £38 participation fee that covers printing, installation and de-installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image. A discount is available to anyone selected for both December exhibitions. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on the shortest side) by free file transfer to the gallery's submissions address. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: Free (£38 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Community Gallery Wall Takeover · Fotografiska Tallinn
item.description: Fotografiska Tallinn invites local and international photographic artists, image-makers, amateur photographers and photography enthusiasts to take over the walls of its Community Gallery on the museum's 1st floor — a space where art, everyday life and lively encounters intersect. The museum is looking for photo series and projects that speak to our time: work that raises timely or socially relevant questions, offers new perspectives and sparks dialogue, and that can enter into conversation with Fotografiska's wider exhibition programme. This first application round closes on 19 August 2026, World Photography Day, and selects work for the autumn 2026 season, when the museum will also present its major Vivian Maier exhibition. After that, submissions remain open year-round, with the next available exhibition slot opening in early 2027. Selected artists present their work in one of Fotografiska Tallinn's most visible and accessible exhibition spaces, supported by the museum's communications, marketing and public programme activities. Both new projects and previously exhibited works are welcome. Production of the works remains the responsibility of the artist, though the museum can recommend trusted production partners. Applications are sent as a single PDF containing 10–15 photographs, a short project description and a short artist bio. — Deadline: August 19, 2026. Fee: Free (production costs if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: F/262 NEXT GEN Award 2026
item.description: Single-image award for young photographers at the F/262 International Photography Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal, run as its own competition alongside the festival's Photography Awards, Curated Open Call and Photo Book Award. Open worldwide to photographers aged 25 and under at the time of submission, split into two bands: Junior (16 and under) enter free and submit 1–3 images; Emerging (17 to 25) pay €5 per image and submit 1–5 images. Both bands must upload proof of age as a PDF. Any subject is welcome and any device qualifies, including analogue cameras and phones; the festival's 2026 sub-theme 'Shaping Shores / Moldar as Margens' is suggested but not required. A shortlist of up to 10 photographers is selected after the deadline. The overall winner takes the title NEXT GEN Photographer of the Year 2026 and a dedicated solo exhibition at the CEF (Centro de Experimentação Fotográfica) in October–November 2026. Gold, Silver and Bronze each receive a festival exhibition plus a Rotary Prize of €450, €200 and €100 respectively, KOYLAB print vouchers of €250, €150 and €100, BlackRapid straps and SmartAlbums software; Gold also receives an Instax Mini Evo Cinema camera. All shortlisted finalists join the NEXT GEN group exhibition and receive a finalist certificate and festival catalogue feature. Photographers keep full copyright; the festival takes a non-exclusive licence for up to three years. Submissions close 19 August 2026, World Photography Day, with the winner announced in September. — Deadline: August 19, 2026. Fee: Free (16 and under) / €5 per image (17–25). Prize: Solo exhibition + €450 Rotary Prize + Instax camera.

item.title: Future of Archives: Whose Archive Is It Anyway? · The Photographers' Gallery
item.description: Open call for speakers for Whose Archive is it Anyway?, a one-day event at The Photographers' Gallery on Friday 16 April 2027 and the first in a three-part series exploring the future of archives and archiving. The brief asks what makes an archive and who decides: who creates one, what it consists of, who it is for, who has access, and what becomes of the everyday material that sits outside institutional collections, hidden, forgotten or displaced. The Gallery is explicit that it wants submissions of real-life experience rather than academic papers, and the call is aimed particularly at people working outside traditional institutions and archives. Suggested subjects include artists' and photographers' legacies, reclaimed photographic archives, family archives, counter-archives that question dominant historical narratives, grassroots and radical archives, questions of ownership and authority over images and their stories, memory and lost histories made visible again, digitisation and digital preservation, and technologies that reduce barriers to archives while safeguarding material. Selected speakers receive a fee of £200. Applicants must be 18 or over and available to attend the Gallery in person on 16 April 2027. There is no application fee. Applying takes a short Microsoft form: name, email, a talk title (which can be a work in progress) and a 400-word summary, plus confirmation that you can present in person on the day. Applications close 1 November 2026 at 11.59pm BST and selected speakers are notified by 18 January 2027. Supported by TownsWeb Archiving. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £200 speaker fee.

item.title: Her Wild Becoming · Visionary Art Collective
item.description: Virtual exhibition and print catalog celebrating the evolving voices of contemporary women artists worldwide, juried by a five-person panel: Danielle Krysa (The Jealous Curator), Ekaterina Popova (Create! Magazine), Alicia Puig (PxP Contemporary), Marina Granger (The Artist Advisory) and Liza Zhurkovskaya (Kefi Art Gallery). The theme reads becoming as an untamed process — identity, intuition, resilience, transformation, and the many ways women define themselves through creative expression — honouring the courage to trust one's inner voice and keep evolving. Open to women artists of all backgrounds, disciplines and experience levels, 18 and over. All 2D and 3D media are accepted, photography named explicitly among them; film and video are not. Selected work appears in the online exhibition on visionaryartcollective.com and in the print catalog, and a small number of artists receive extra prizes from the jurors (a Substack subscription, Create! Collective membership, a Create! Magazine blog feature and two Instagram spotlights). Tiered fees: $25 for 1–2 images, $30 for 3–4, $35 for 5–6. Artists are notified within four to six weeks of the deadline and the exhibition is presented in October 2026. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: $25–35. Prize: Virtual exhibition + print catalog.

item.title: Solo and Small Group Exhibits · The Delaplaine Arts Center
item.description: The Delaplaine seeks proposals for solo and small group exhibitions on an ongoing basis, for five galleries on two floors of its building in historic downtown Frederick, Maryland; openings are held on most first Saturdays. Proposals go to an Exhibition Selection Panel of artists, art professionals, art consultants and art educators, which asks whether the work is enriching, cohesive and relevant, and whether the installation suits the spaces available — the Delaplaine states plainly that artists are not judged on their backgrounds or writing skills. All media are encouraged and the call is open to anyone: past exhibitors have been local and international, professional and non-professional, self-taught and highly trained. Applicants submit 6–20 work samples with a bio/CV, artist statement and exhibit proposal; no commercially made prints, giclées or reproductions of an original work are considered. Proposals are reviewed every other month (received Jan 15–Mar 14, notified by Apr 8; Mar 15–May 14 by Jun 8; May 15–Jul 14 by Aug 8; Jul 15–Sep 14 by Oct 8; Sep 15–Nov 14 by Dec 8; Nov 15–Jan 14 by Feb 8), and shows are scheduled about two years in advance, which gives artists room to develop the body of work they intend to exhibit. Fees are $7 for Delaplaine members and $37 for non-members — the figure the Delaplaine's own FAQ and the CaFÉ prospectus text both give, though CaFÉ's fee panel prints $35 for non-members, so budget for the higher one. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $37 ($7 members). Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Capturing Ecology 2026 · British Ecological Society
item.description: The British Ecological Society's annual photography competition, run since 2013, looks for images that tell ecological stories — triumph, challenge and survival — rather than pretty wildlife portraits alone. The 2026 edition opens eight categories: Ecologists in Action (yourself or colleagues at work in the field or lab), Animals (in partnership with ZSL), Plants and Fungi (with Plantlife), Species Interactions, Resilient Nature, Doorstep Ecology, Macro Photography, and a new Nature from Above category for drone and aerial work. Entrants may submit up to eight images, each with full camera settings, location, species names and a description of what is happening; no image may be entered in two categories. A panel of wildlife photographers and ecologists — Max Mudie, Ian Price, Gabriela Staebler, Laura Dyer, Matt Doggett, Rathika Ramasamy, Richard Bardgett and Harriet McAra — scores every entry on creativity, impact and technical merit, and the BES makes the final call. The overall winner takes £750 and twelve months of free BES membership; each category winner takes £120, and one person may win at most two categories. Entry is free for BES members and is waived entirely for photographers who are citizens of and resident in a Global South country; everyone else pays £12 per entry. Plantlife members may enter the Plants and Fungi category free. Digital enhancement must be declared and is limited to cleaning and minor colour work — black and white is fine, AI-generated images are not accepted, and animal welfare, honesty and permits are treated as disqualifying rules rather than guidance. Photographers retain copyright; entering grants the BES and its partners the right to reproduce the work, including in its membership magazine Niche. Under-18s are actively encouraged to enter. Submissions close at 23:59 BST on Monday 31 August 2026 and winners are announced in January 2027. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: £12 (BES members & Global South free). Prize: £750 + £120 per category.

item.title: Art and the Ship Channel · Art League of Baytown
item.description: The Art League of Baytown's first fall juried exhibition, funded by the Port Houston Community Grant Program and built around the communities, parks and green spaces within three miles of the Houston Ship Channel. Photography is one of three judged categories alongside 2D and 3D work, and the source of inspiration must be a public park, greenspace or publicly accessible community within that three-mile band — private property is off limits, though neither the organiser's page nor the ArtCall prospectus states a residency rule — the three-mile band governs the subject of the work, not where the artist lives. Awards total $2,000: $300 Best of Show and a $200 Honoree Award chosen by a Port Houston representative, plus $175 first, $150 second, $100 third and a $75 honourable mention in each of the three categories. Donna Tennant jurors the show. Work must have been made in the past five years, be entirely the artist's own, and carry a short artist statement that is displayed alongside it; copies of other people's work, images built from published or copyrighted photographs, and AI-generated art are all ineligible, as is work depicting nudes, destruction, cruelty, political statements or violence. Photographs must be framed unless printed on canvas or metal, wired and ready to hang, and no larger than 48 x 48 inches; no sawtooth hangers. Judging weighs visual impact, originality, composition and craftsmanship, with a further criterion for resourceful and sustainable use of materials. Entries run 1 August to 16 September 2026 through ArtCall, acceptance emails go out between 26 and 30 September, and accepted work is delivered in person in Baytown on 8–9 October (other arrangements by email if those dates are impossible). The show runs 10–30 October, Thursdays to Saturdays, closing with an awards reception on 30 October. Sale is preferred but not required; the Art League retains a 20% commission. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: $30 first entry + $15 each addl (up to 3). Prize: $2,000 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Booker Creek Arts Festival 2026
item.description: The inaugural Booker Creek Arts Festival turns St. Petersburg's historic EDGE District into a four-day walkable gallery from 12 to 15 November 2026, with juried work by hundreds of Florida artists hung inside the district's restaurants, cafés, shops, hotels and residential buildings rather than in a single venue. Named after the urban stream that runs through downtown St. Petersburg, the festival wraps the art in live mural painting, glass blowing, dance, music and children's activities, and visitors move between venues with a map, voting by text for the People's Choice Award. Up to $50,000 in prizes is on offer — a $10,000 Booker Creek Best of Show, a $7,500 Award of Excellence, ten $1,500 Merit Awards and two $2,500 People's Choice Awards, presented on Saturday 14 November. The organisers name painting, photography, wall sculpture and mixed media among the competing media, and entries may be paintings, sculptures, ceramic works, textile works, photographs, drawings, mixed-media works, collages or assemblages. Entry is open to artists who have lived in Florida for at least six consecutive months and are 18 or older on 14 August 2026; each artist makes one application only, submitting three separate works with one high-resolution image each, for a $25 non-refundable fee. Every submitted work must have been completed in or after 2023 and must be physically hangable — digital-only works, new media, video and film are not permitted, and a single piece may occupy no more than 6 feet high by 8 feet wide. Work created solely by AI software will not be treated as the artist's own and will be disqualified. Artists do not have to be present during the festival, and visitors can buy work directly from them. Submissions close at 11:59pm EDT on Friday 14 August 2026. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: $25 (3 works). Prize: $10,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Freedom: The Spirit Within · Marion Cultural Alliance
item.description: Marion Cultural Alliance's September 2026 juried exhibition, presented, curated and juried by Lisa Russo (M.F.A., M.Ed.), asks artists what freedom means to them — personal journeys, creative expression, relationships, beliefs, memories and everyday life. Work responding to America's 250th anniversary and the 25th anniversary of September 11 is welcome but the theme is deliberately wider, taking in self-expression, resilience, identity, hope, possibility, remembrance and the enduring human spirit. The call is open to local and regional artists in all media, with photography named alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, fibre art, mixed media, digital art and fine craft; MCA membership is not required to enter. Each artist may submit up to two original pieces, no giclées or reproductions, suggested size up to 50 inches in any direction, and only work that engages the theme will be accepted. Cash and ribbon awards go to Best of Show, which carries the cash prize, with ribbons for first through fifth place and honourable mention. All exhibited work must be for sale, with proceeds split 70% to the artist and 30% to MCA, whose share funds its arts programming in Ocala and Marion County. Alongside the show, guest curator Lisa Russo runs a hands-on classical drawing workshop, Draw Like the Masters, on Saturday 19 September 2026 — a separate, optional $75 booking. Entries are submitted digitally through ArtCall by midnight on Sunday 16 August 2026; no physical or mailed submissions are accepted. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $25 (1 work), $35 (2 works). Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Art & Woman Edition 4 · Arts to Hearts Project
item.description: The fourth volume of Arts to Hearts Project's Art & Woman series, a storytelling-based publishing project that has published more than 300 women artists since 2024. Guest curator for this edition is Liz Lidgett, founder of Liz Lidgett Gallery and Design in Des Moines and author of Art for Everyone. The edition is intentionally open-themed: rather than responding to a set concept, artists are asked to submit work that reflects their own journey and practice, whether that means identity, memory, belonging, resilience, transformation, family, culture, motherhood, healing, loss or joy. Submissions are welcome across all visual media, with photography named alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics, textile art, mixed media, collage, digital art, installation, illustration and experimental practice, and there is no requirement to make new work — existing, previously exhibited or already sold pieces are eligible so long as the artist holds the rights. The top winner receives a USD $500 cash award, a four-page editorial feature in the book, a written artist interview on the Arts to Hearts site, an engraved crystal trophy and certificate, and newsletter and social promotion to the project's audience; the first runner-up also receives a four-page feature, an interview and a trophy, and the second runner-up a four-page feature and a trophy. A separate optional $22 add-on buys a published virtual studio-visit interview if selected; it is not part of the entry. The book is distributed worldwide through Amazon, Barnes & Noble and the Arts to Hearts shop. Open to women and womxn artists worldwide aged 18 or over at any career stage, including collaborative work where the submitting artist identifies as a woman. Entry is tiered by image count, from $21 for one image to $100 for twenty. Applications close at 11:59pm EST on 30 August 2026. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 (tiered, 1–20 images). Prize: $500 + Publication.

item.title: Art in the Atrium 26 · City of Frisco Cultural Affairs
item.description: The 26th installment of the City of Frisco's Art in the Atrium, a free rotating exhibition in the atrium of the George A. Purefoy Municipal Center. The city seeks original two-dimensional work from artists in Frisco and the surrounding area, loaned for display from 30 September 2026 to 1 February 2027. Photographs are explicitly provided for and must be printed on quality paper at a resolution of at least 300 dpi; work must have been made within the past two years, be framed and ready to hang with wire securely attached — unframed canvases with finished edges and wire are also accepted — and measure no more than 60 by 60 inches. Three-dimensional work is not considered. Each artist may submit two images through CaFÉ at no cost, with a description explaining motivation, themes or process, and pieces may be offered for sale. Submissions are reviewed by the Arts and Culture Advisory Board and city staff on criteria including uniqueness and originality, visual impact and demonstrated excellence of technique, and every artist is notified in writing. Work must be delivered and collected in person, with drop-off on 29 September 2026 — shipped work is not accepted and return shipping is not provided. The entry deadline is Wednesday 6 September 2026. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Teeny Tiny BOLD · Ripple Artspace
item.description: Ripple Artspace — formerly Rountree Gallery, on Main Street in Platteville, Wisconsin — runs Teeny Tiny BOLD as its annual national juried exhibition of small-scale work. Working within a limited scale, the gallery argues, forces artists to distil ideas and refine craft, and the call is open to all subjects and themes in any medium provided the finished piece measures no more than 12 inches in any direction including frame, base or mounting hardware. Photography is named among the eligible media alongside painting, drawing, collage, fibre, metal, ceramics, sculpture, printmaking, mixed media and digital media; both two- and three-dimensional work is welcome. The juror is John T. Upchurch, a Chicago-based sculptor working in wood, stone, metal, found objects and salvaged material who earned his BFA from the Kansas City Art Institute in 1990. The exhibition runs 19 November 2026 to 9 January 2027 and is marked by three public events: Small Business Saturday and Holiday Magic on Main on 28 November, an Artist Sunday open house with live music from the Prairie Lights String Band on 29 November, and an artist reception on 11 December. Ripple Artspace retains a 30% commission on all work sold during the exhibition, and sold pieces stay on the wall until it closes. AI-generated work is not eligible and may be disqualified. Open to artists aged 18 or older residing in the United States or its territories; the entry fee is $30 for three to six images. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $30 (3 images), $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Bettie Awards 2027 · The Delaplaine Arts Center
item.description: The Elizabeth Barker Delaplaine Award for Young Artists — the Bettie Awards — is the Delaplaine Arts Center's annual free award for high-school artists, run each March for Youth Art Month and named for a lifelong supporter of the arts in Frederick County, Maryland. Artists living in or attending school in Frederick County in grades 9 to 12, whether public, private or homeschooled, may apply at no cost with one work no more than five feet in any direction; all media are eligible, photography named alongside painting, printmaking, ceramics, drawing and sculpture. A first-round jury of Delaplaine instructors and art professionals selects at least ten Bettie Award Winners, and a second-round jury of artists from across the region picks one of them as the Bettie Award Grand Prize Winner. The grand prize is $1,000; every other winner receives $100, and visitors vote through the run of the show for a People's Choice Award worth $250. The grand prize winner is also featured in an article in Delaplaine Arts magazine, distributed across the region, and other winners' work may be published in local print and online media. Judges treat presentation as a real criterion and will not award the grand prize to work that is poorly prepared for installation. Applications close at 11:59pm EST on Monday 1 February 2027, winners are announced on 6 February, selected work is delivered 22–28 February, and the exhibition opens with an awards presentation on Saturday 6 March 2027, running to 25 April. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Eerie Expressions · San Marcos Art League
item.description: The San Marcos Art League's October show at the San Marcos Art Center, asking for work that captures the spirit of the month — spooky, scary, black-light, Goth-inspired, spirits and monsters and goblins, from the whimsical to the wonderfully dark. Entry is open to all and every medium is eligible, with photographs and digital art named explicitly alongside fine art prints, sculpture, textiles and pottery. Each artist may enter one original work completed in the last 24 months and not previously shown at the Art Center Gallery. Two-dimensional work must be framed or gallery-wrapped with no visible staples and wired for the gallery's hanging system — no saw-tooth hangers — and no larger than 36 by 68 inches including the frame; three-dimensional work is judged on size and stability and must stand unaided. Subject matter has to suit a family-oriented venue. All work is hand-delivered — the Art Center does not accept shipments — with intake on 4 October between 1pm and 4pm, a public reception on 9 October from 7 to 9pm (an hour later than usual, to find the darkness), and pickup on 29–30 October. Work must be for sale at a price fixed at entry and the Art League retains a 20% commission. Entry is $10 for Art League members using the code emailed to them and $20 otherwise; submissions close 2 October at 5pm or when the show fills. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: $20 ($10 members). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Hounds in the Hulse · Art Center Waco
item.description: A free community exhibition in the Hulse Gallery at Art Center Waco built entirely from work about pets and companion animals — furry, feathered, scaled or otherwise. The centre addresses the call to pet lovers throughout McLennan County and the surrounding area, and is explicit that you do not have to be a professional artist to take part: it welcomes submissions from artists at every level, from community members, and from pet owners who commissioned a portrait of their animal. Every medium is eligible and photography is named alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, fibre art, sculpture and ceramics, so long as the work features or is inspired by a pet. Each person may submit up to three artworks through the centre's Google Form, with no entry fee. Work must arrive ready to display safely in a gallery: there is no minimum size, nothing may exceed 72 inches in any direction, wall pieces are capped at 60 pounds, and framed work needs secure hanging hardware. Gallery space is limited, so submitting does not guarantee inclusion — Art Center Waco says it will show as many community submissions as it can while keeping the hang safe and considered. Selected participants are sent drop-off, exhibition and pickup details afterwards. Submissions close 31 August 2026. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Mosaic Life Care Juried Exhibition · Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art
item.description: Mosaic Life Care and the Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art run this judged exhibition together for artists living within 100 miles of St. Joseph, Missouri. Selected work hangs in the Art Experience Galleries at Mosaic Life Care from 2 September 2026 and stays up for roughly six months unless it sells. Work is judged with ribbons awarded across ten categories, photography and digital art among them alongside oil and acrylic, watercolour, drawing, printmaking, ceramics, 2-D mixed media, fibre and textiles, and sculpture and 3-D mixed media; awards are announced at the opening reception. One $30 entry fee covers an unlimited number of works. Entries go to the Albrecht-Kemper Museum by post or email with a signed entry form, a completed W-9 and a separate photograph of each piece — JPEG files under 1MB named artist, entry number, title and medium, or printed photos of at least 4x6 inches labelled on the back — and the fee is paid online through the museum's call-for-artists page. Entrants under 18 need a parent or guardian signature. Work must be original and the artist's sole property, free of others' copyrighted material, and pieces shown in a previous Mosaic exhibition are not eligible; subject matter depicting cemeteries, death, violence, blood, car crashes or nudity is barred, and the venue cannot accommodate video or performance work. Work is priced at entry and the Albrecht-Kemper Museum takes a 30% commission, with the artist supplying a comparable replacement if a piece sells before the six months are up. Entries close 11:59pm CT on Friday 7 August 2026, with artists notified on 14 August and accepted work delivered on 1 September. — Deadline: August 7, 2026. Fee: $30 (unlimited works). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Quiet Landscape: Beauty, Stillness, and Connection · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: PhotoPlace Gallery's autumn juried call for landscape photographs that reward slowing down. Rather than dramatic spectacle, the gallery is looking for pictures that invite reflection and reveal the subtle relationships between people, place, light and time — sweeping vistas and intimate details, untouched wilderness and cultivated fields. Natural, rural, urban and cultivated landscapes are all welcome, approached through traditional, documentary, conceptual or fine-art methods, and work may turn on solitude, atmosphere, changing seasons or the quiet moments that usually go unnoticed. Juror Kat Kiernan, formerly editor-in-chief of Don't Take Pictures and now Manager of Public Programs at the Morgan Library & Museum, will select up to 35 photographs for the gallery in Middlebury, Vermont and roughly 40 more for the online gallery. All selected work is reproduced in the exhibition catalog, kept permanently on the PhotoPlace website and promoted through the gallery's publications and social channels; online-gallery selections receive the same catalog inclusion and promotion as the wall selections, and all selected artists are eligible for exhibition awards. Entries open 8 August 2026 and close 7 September, with juror selections announced 21 September, prints due 23 October and the show running 6–28 November 2026 with an opening reception on 6 November. There is no limit on the number of images submitted. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: $39 (5 images) + $6 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.
